title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 25
description: Ten questions on Acts 25: Festus in Caesarea, Paul's appeal to Caesar, and the hearing arranged before King Agrippa.

questions.text: Where did Festus go up, three days after coming into the province?
questions.explanation: Festus, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

answers.text: To Jerusalem
To Antioch
To Rome
To Malta

questions.text: What were the leading men plotting when they asked Festus to summon Paul to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: They asked a favor against Paul, that Festus would summon him to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way.

answers.text: To make him swear by the temple
To hand him over to the Romans
To kill him on the way
To take his money as a fine

questions.text: What did Paul say in his defense when the charges were brought?
questions.explanation: Paul said he had not sinned at all against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar.

answers.text: That he had sinned against the temple only in ignorance
That he had sinned neither against the law, nor the temple, nor Caesar
That he had never once gone up to the city of Jerusalem
That the law of the Jews did not apply to him

questions.text: What did Festus ask Paul, desiring to gain favor with the Jews?
questions.explanation: Festus asked Paul whether he was willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by him there concerning these things.

answers.text: Whether he would pay for his release
Whether he would deny the resurrection
Whether he would leave the province quietly
Whether he was willing to be judged at Jerusalem

questions.text: What did Paul declare at the end of his answer to Festus?
questions.explanation: Paul said that if the charges were untrue no one could give him up to them, and he declared, "I appeal to Caesar!"

answers.text: "I appeal to the council!"
"I will go up to Jerusalem."
"I appeal to Caesar!"
"Let the high priest judge me."

questions.text: Who arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus after some days had passed?
questions.explanation: When some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.

answers.text: King Agrippa and Bernice
Felix and Drusilla
Claudius Lysias and Tertullus
Julius and Aristarchus

questions.text: What did Festus say was not the custom of the Romans?
questions.explanation: Festus said it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense.

answers.text: To judge a prisoner outside the city where he was seized
To hear a case without the high priest being present
To send a prisoner to the emperor for a decision
To give up a man before he has faced his accusers and defended himself

questions.text: What did Festus say Paul affirmed about one Jesus?
questions.explanation: Festus said the questions were about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

answers.text: That Jesus had never died
That Jesus, who was dead, was alive
That Jesus would judge Caesar
That Jesus was a teacher of the law

questions.text: What did Agrippa say to Festus about the prisoner?
questions.explanation: Agrippa said he would also like to hear the man himself, and Festus said he would hear him the next day.

answers.text: That he should be sent to Jerusalem
That he should be released at once
That he would also like to hear the man himself
That he had no interest in the case

questions.text: Why did Festus bring Paul out before Agrippa and the others?
questions.explanation: Festus said he had nothing certain to write to his lord, so he brought Paul out that after examination he might have something to write, since it seemed unreasonable to send a prisoner without specifying the charges.

answers.text: So that after examination he might have something to write
So that Agrippa could pronounce the sentence
So that the crowd could see the prisoner
So that the chief priests could accuse him again
